note: Oral S1P1 modulators (ozanimod, etrasimod) for moderate-to-severe UC, developed on mouse colitis models with peripheral lymphocyte count as the engagement readout.
label: Ulcerative colitis (S1P)

engagement.note: FTY720 sequestered circulating lymphocytes in lymphoid tissue of colitic IL-10-/- mice; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: FTY720 sequesters lymphocytes in colitic mice
engagement.quote: Single-dose administration of FTY720 resulted in the sequestration of circulating lymphocytes within the secondary lymphoid tissues.

engagement.note: Ozanimod reversibly cut circulating B and CCR7+ T cells in rodents; UC patients' lymphocytes fell 32-49% in TOUCHSTONE.
engagement.quote: At week 8, absolute lymphocyte counts declined 49% from baseline in the group that received 1 mg of ozanimod and 32% from baseline in the group that received 0.5 mg.
engagement.reason: Lymphocytes fell in patients as in rodents
engagement.judgement: Juxtaposed Scott 2016 (rodents, DOI 10.1111/bph.13476: 'induced a reversible reduction in circulating B and CCR7+ T lymphocytes in vivo') with TOUCHSTONE; no primary source puts rodent and patient counts side by side, and the rodent magnitude is not in the abstract, so direction only. Healthy-volunteer FIH (Tran 2017, DOI 10.1002/jcph.887) gave a 65-68% median fall at 1-1.5 mg. Sugahara 2017 (DOI 10.1111/bph.13641) does state a rat/monkey-to-human comparison for amiselimod, but in healthy volunteers and amiselimod has no UC result.

dose.model: Rodent PK and lymphocyte PD (ozanimod); mouse concentration-lymphocyte curve (etrasimod)
dose.note: Rodent PK and lymphocyte PD set once-daily dosing; no published test of a rodent exposure target against patient exposure.
dose.short: Rodent PK-lymphocyte curve never tested in patients
dose.quote: RPC1063 showed high oral bioavailability and volume of distribution, and a circulatory half-life that supports once daily dosing.
dose.judgement: Al-Shamma 2019 (DOI 10.1124/jpet.118.254268) reports 'A dose-dependent relationship was observed for etrasimod plasma concentration and lymphocyte count in mice' but no human comparison. Clinical doses were set from healthy-volunteer lymphocyte PD (Tran 2017 for ozanimod; etrasimod SAD/MAD, DOI 10.1002/cpdd.1379). Abstract-level reading only; Scott 2016 full text was not retrievable from PMC.

efficacy.note: FTY720 ameliorated established colitis in IL-10-/- mice; fingolimod was never trialled in UC.
efficacy.short: FTY720 heals colitis in IL-10-/- mice
efficacy.quote: Treatment of established colitis in IL-10-/- mice with FTY720 ameliorated the colitis, probably as a result of decreasing the number of lymphocytes in the colonic mucosa and an associated reduction in IFN-gamma production.

efficacy.note: Ozanimod cleared both mouse colitis models; TOUCHSTONE then gave 16% vs 6% remission at week 8, confirmed in TRUE NORTH 2021 and ELEVATE 2023.
efficacy.quote: In this preliminary trial, ozanimod at a daily dose of 1 mg resulted in a slightly higher rate of clinical remission of ulcerative colitis than placebo.
efficacy.reason: Mouse colitis cleared; patients reached remission
efficacy.judgement: Model side from Scott 2016: 'Oral RPC1063 reduced inflammation and disease parameters in all three autoimmune disease models.' Juxtaposed, not a stated comparison. Later same-direction confirmations: TRUE NORTH (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2033617, 18.4% vs 6.0%, registry results 2021-09-01) and ELEVATE UC 52/12 for etrasimod (DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00061-2, registry results 2022-12-20/21; Al-Shamma 2019 used the CD45RBhi model). Not 'neg': the model flagged no failure. Not 'contra': KRP-203 cleared IL-10-/- colitis (Song 2008, DOI 10.1124/jpet.106.119172) and its UC proof-of-concept NCT01375179 was terminated at 27 patients with no posted results and no primary publication retrieved; amiselimod's phase 2 failure was in Crohn's disease, not UC, and its UC phase 2 NCT04857112 (completed 2024-11) has no results posted and no publication found.

safety.note: Mouse genetics assigned bradycardia to S1P3, predicting S1P1-selective agonists would spare heart rate.
safety.quote: The sustained bradycardia induced by S1P receptor non-selective immunosuppressive agonists in wild-type mice is abolished in S1P3-/- mice, whereas S1P1-selective agonist does not produce bradycardia.

safety.note: Siponimod spares S1P3, which mouse genetics tied to bradycardia, yet slowed human hearts on day 1 via atrial GIRK; ozanimod and etrasimod did too.
safety.quote: Despite sparing S1P3 receptors (associated with bradycardia in mice), BAF312 induced rapid, transient (day 1 only) bradycardia in humans.
safety.reason: Mouse S1P3 rule failed in humans
safety.judgement: Class-level contradiction with a stated species comparison; siponimod is a class proxy (MS drug, healthy volunteers). Carried into UC drugs: ozanimod FIH (Tran 2017, DOI 10.1002/jcph.887) 'A dose-dependent negative chronotropic effect was observed following the first dose'; etrasimod SAD/MAD (DOI 10.1002/cpdd.1379) first-dose falls up to 19.5 bpm; both healthy volunteers. The replacement model, human atrial-myocyte GIRK activation plus monkey telemetry, predicted amiselimod's lack of first-dose bradycardia and was confirmed in healthy subjects (Sugahara 2017, DOI 10.1111/bph.13641; Harada 2017, DOI 10.1111/bcp.13203), but amiselimod has no UC result, so it does not lift the contra. Patient-level bradycardia rates in TRUE NORTH/ELEVATE are not in the abstracts read.
